sources.entry: James - Open-source proxy tool for checking and mapping requests with http as well as https. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/james-proxy/james) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: James is an open-source HTTP and HTTPS proxy and monitor, built with hoxy, Electron and React, for viewing, intercepting and mapping browser requests.
summary.what_it_does: James sits between a browser and the web as an HTTP proxy, letting developers view and intercept requests made from the browser. It supports URL mappings where a "url to map" field can use "*" wildcards between adjacent slashes, and multiple wildcards can be used in one URL. HTTPS proxying is supported but requires following setup instructions in the project wiki. The README describes it as an open-source alternative to the Charles developer tool. The app is built with hoxy, Electron and React, and the README lists npm scripts for tests, lint, building and creating standalone bundles.
use_cases: inspect HTTP traffic from a browser
map or redirect URLs during development
how_to_run: Download the correct version for your OS and run
notable: Wildcard URL mappings using '*' between slashes
Electron app that reloads on code changes during development
Positioned as an open-source alternative to Charles
Standalone app bundles via npm run release
caveats: README states the project is in maintenance mode and the original team has limited time
HTTPS support needs extra setup described in the wiki
The README suggests HTTP Toolkit as an actively maintained alternative
